data.standardized_narrative: During 2015 the syndicate recorded a prioryear release: the net provision for claims included a release of GBP 17.8m. Management attribute this principally to favourable claims development in longtail casualty classes (notably reductions in the assessment of thirdparty liability claims on 2013 and earlier years) together with a release of catastrophe loadings as policies come off risk. While Superstorm Sandy and earlier international catastrophe events remain significant gross exposures, recent runoff experience has been overall beneficial to prior years.
raw_causal_phrases: a release of catastrophe loads on 2014 year of account as policies come off risk
a reduction in the assessment of third party liability claims on the 2013 and prior accounts following lower than expected incurred claims movements during 2015
The movement in the net provision for claims includes a release of GBP 17.8m in respect of claims outstanding at the previous year end (2014: GBP 22.8m).
long-tail casualty classes account for around 70% of the back-year release

data.data_quality_notes: Gross prioryear movement (GROSS PYD) was not explicitly provided. The report explicitly states a net release of GBP 17.8m (used above). The gross change in total claims outstanding from 31/12/2014 to 31/12/2015 equals a GBP 21.237m release (342.270  321.033), but that movement includes current year activity. A gross 'movement in prior years' note was not unambiguously provided, and RITC activity (acceptances from Syndicate 6103) may distort some development tables. Prioryear event amounts (e.g. Sandy, 2010/11 cats) were reported as gross estimates but often not reconciled to a single gross PYD figure; therefore net figure from the note was used per instructions and flagged.
